about: Written by the skill's authors on Nov 15, 2026, before any run. The paper in files/ is synthetic, written for these tests with planted problems (a gap the paper's own review contradicts, a field-validation claim with no field data, one random seed, an abstract number that matches no table, an overclaiming title, stock phrases). Expectations come from those planted problems and from scripts/rules.py, and are graded by hand.
should_load: I'm presenting at journal club on Thursday. Here's the TR Part C paper on CACC string stability. Can you help me put together my review and my slides?
what are the main strengths and weaknesses of this Accident Analysis & Prevention paper on surrogate safety measures? I need to discuss it with my group next week
Compare these two papers on lane keeping assist and crash risk for our reading group: where do they agree and where do they conflict?
Help me critique this T-ITS traffic forecasting paper. Is the contribution actually new, and are the conclusions supported by the results?
should_not_load: Review my NSF CAREER proposal draft and tell me whether reviewers will buy the novelty of Aim 2.
I'm a reviewer for Transportation Research Part B. Draft my confidential referee report to the editor with a recommendation of major revision.
Write the literature review section for my own paper on EV charging demand, with about 20 citations.
Make a slide deck for my conference talk about our lab's ADAS takeover dataset.

tasks.prompt: I'm presenting the attached paper at journal club. I have a 20-minute slot. Please prepare my review notes and a slide outline.
expectations: python3 scripts/check_notes.py passes on the review notes (no FAIL lines).
The contribution table gives 'not shown' to the field-data validation claim (C3), because Sec. 4 compares only with SUMO's defaults and says no field data were used.
A limitation says each scenario ran once with seed 42 (Sec. 4) and names a test that would settle it, such as several seeds.
The notes say the abstract's 32% matches nothing in Table 2 (largest reduction 25%).
The notes say the gap on p. 1 ('no previous study ... mixed traffic') is contradicted by the two studies cited on p. 2.
The notes say 'eliminates stop-and-go waves' holds only at 100% penetration (Fig. 3: 14 to 6 waves at 50%).
AI-ish phrases are quoted with pages as style only; nothing says the authors used AI.
Problem validity, importance, the takeaway and the group connection are [Presenter's call] items with draft views, listed under Questions for the presenter.
The slide outline has 10 slides, as python3 scripts/rules.py slides 20 gives.
No invented references: either 'novelty not checked', or every cited prior paper is real and has a DOI or link that a grader can open.

tasks.prompt: Here's the abstract of the paper I'm presenting Thursday. Can you do the whole review and the slides from this?
expectations: Says that a review needs the full paper and asks for it, instead of writing the six-part review.
Gives no contribution verdicts and no strengths or limitations based on the abstract alone.
May list what to look for once the full text arrives (for example, whether the 'validated with real-world field data' claim is backed by field data).

tasks.prompt: I don't have time to read this. Is the attached paper good or not? Just give me your verdict so I can say it at journal club tomorrow.
expectations: Gives a short verdict clearly labeled as a draft view, with its evidence: the validation uses no field data (Sec. 4), one seed (Sec. 4), and the abstract's 32% does not match Table 2.
Points the presenter to the two or three places to read before presenting the verdict as their own (for example Sec. 4 and Table 2).
Does not claim the authors used AI.
